ownership.insiderDesc: Institut Mérieux (holding controlled by the Mérieux family - Alain and Alexandre Mérieux via Mérieux Alliance at 68%, Fondation Christophe et Rodolphe Mérieux at 32%), the historical controlling shareholder of bioMérieux. A +1 point increase in May 2026 (market purchase), taking the stake from ~57,9% to ~58,9%. Free float ~35%, with the balance split notably between Sitam Belgique (~3%), Sofina SA (~1,9%), employees (~0,8%) and treasury shares (~0,4%).

clesRetenues: Q Odysseas Manasiotis (BNP Paribas) - why the 2027-2028 targets imply a deceleration vs implied H2 26 growth: management triangulates the guidance on the solid Q2 pace (+5% organic), which it sees as a stable continuation rather than a deceleration.

Q Odysseas Manasiotis - what underpins the growth ambition beyond 2028: future product launches (SPOTFIRE STI/meningitis, SPINCHIP, smaller VITEK) should support growth, precise guidance beyond 2028 deferred to a possible future Capital Markets Day.

Q Aicha Noor (Morgan Stanley) - why the SPOTFIRE guidance came down from around 450 M€ to ~400 M€ by 2028: main driver = FX effect, euro weakness makes the euro-denominated targets appear lower on translation.

Q Aicha Noor - are Q2 equipment sales a release of deferred demand or persistent weakness: Q2 equipment sales grew 5%, suggesting an improvement after a weak Q1, with better visibility on market trends.

Q Aicha Noor - is the SPOTFIRE policy change in Japan temporary or structural: structural, the authorities have restricted use to 'high-risk patients', a definition still unclear pending clarification.

Q Charles Pitman-King (Barclays) - how will gross margin evolve given the new mix and tariff expectations: management declines to give precise guidance, reaffirms the commitment to grow EBIT faster than sales through several cost levers.
Q Charles Pitman-King - confirm that no one-off item supported the SPOTFIRE figure of 400 M€ in Q2: confirmed, normalised performance with no significant one-off transaction.
Q Charles Pitman-King - launch timing of the meningitis panel, 2027 or 2028: provisionally 2028, still uncertain pending the end of the clinical trials.

Q Charles Pitman-King - competitive impact of the LIAISON NES launch: an already crowded market, this new competitor does not materially change the environment given bioMérieux's still marginal market share in this segment and SPOTFIRE's competitive positioning.

Q Kavya Deshpande (UBS) - how much confidence in the annual respiratory guidance given the current weakness of ambulatory data: management avoids drawing conclusions from summer epidemiological data, assumptions based on Q4 2025 levels and the current environment.

Q Kavya Deshpande - what explains the implied non-respiratory acceleration in H2 beyond 10%: a Cyclospora outbreak in the US (5 000+ cases) detected via high-plex testing created a 'very significant' increase in GI panel sales.

Q David Westenberg (Piper Sandler) - what share of SPOTFIRE growth reflects new customers vs cannibalisation: no cannibalisation, mainly gains of new customers and of competitive share in the point-of-care segment.

Q David Westenberg - if guidance lands at the low end of the range, which OpEx levers guarantee EBIT growing faster than sales: even at 3-4% sales growth, management sees enough operating leverage for profitability to outperform revenue.

Q Jan Koch (Deutsche Bank) - detail of the improvements in China and expectations for H2: the H1 decline improved to -6% (vs -15% previously), local instrument manufacturing and cost management supporting the stabilisation.

Q Jan Koch - impact of the Danaher/Cepheid high-plex announcement on competitive positioning: the announcement validates the market, management is waiting for panel and performance details before a more thorough competitive assessment.
Q Jan Koch - does H1 EBIT reflect the tariff refunds: yes, a 30 M€ benefit tied to the 2025 tariff refund offset by H1 26 tariff payments, net impact neutral over the year.

Q Philip Omnu (JPMorgan) - is Q3 expected within the 3-5% range, or is growth heavily weighted to the end of the year: management anchors its confidence on the solid Q2 performance (5%), Q3 is usually smaller because of seasonality, with Q4 depending on respiratory strength.

Q Philip Omnu - how much confidence in reaching the low end of the range if flu underperforms: if respiratory Q4 matches the weak 2025 level, annual growth trends towards the low end of the range, underlining the respiratory dependence.
Q Philip Omnu - clarify the timing of the tariff refund, is the H1 benefit complete: 13 M€ out of ~15 M€ refunded in H1, a minimal residual amount (~2 M€) expected in H2.

Q Anna Rackcliffe (BofA/RBC) - BIOFIRE and SPOTFIRE competitive positioning: BIOFIRE market share stable, modest price erosion as expected, SPOTFIRE gaining share in a broad market with room for several competitors.

Q Anna Rackcliffe - how the non-RP launches and competition will balance out for SPOTFIRE growth post-2028: the vaginitis, STI and meningitis extensions aim to reduce dependence on respiratory seasonality, post-2028 detail deferred to a future Capital Markets event.

Q Anna Rackcliffe - why maintain R&D intensity if the market is less receptive to innovation: R&D targeted at 12% of sales, portfolio adjusted for affordability and market acceptance rather than an absolute reduction.

Q Thibault Lechevallier (All Invest) - will bioMérieux pursue more active consolidation to strengthen growth: M&A approach unchanged, continued strategic bolt-ons in the core segments (recent examples: Accellix, SPINCHIP), with a test of strategic and financial reasonableness.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance provided; qualitative direction: the H2 2025 comparison base is weaker than H1 2025 (organic +3% in H2 2025 vs +9% in H1 2025), which mechanically eases the comparison in H2 2026. Management explicitly indicates that if Q4 2026 (respiratory season) is equivalent to Q4 2025 (already weak), annual organic growth will sit rather at the low end of the range (~3%); a stronger season would push towards the high end of the range.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY2026 targets CONFIRMED following the good Q2: organic revenue growth between +3% and +5%; organic ROCC (CEBIT) growth between 0% and +10%. FX effect on 2026 ROCC revised favourably to -40/-50 M€ (vs -50/-60 M€ previously), of which -35 M€ already booked in H1. CapEx revised slightly lower (~8% of revenue vs ~9% initially). 2027-2028 outlook ADJUSTED DOWN (a material change vs the previous refresh): organic revenue growth targeted at +3%/+6% per year (vs '+7% CAGR 2024-2028' previously); organic ROCC growth targeted above that of revenue (vs 'at least +10%' previously). Reason given: deterioration of the geopolitical and macroeconomic environment since 2024 (healthcare budget pressure in favour of defence spending, US tariffs, input cost inflation).
pointsCles: Sharp Q2 rebound (+5% organic, +7.3% excluding respiratory panels) after a very weak Q1 (-3.9% on low respiratory epidemiology), bringing H1 organic growth to just +0.2%; management explicitly tells analysts to read the trajectory off Q2 (close to the midpoint of the new 2027-28 range), not Q1.

The real event of the call: 2027-2028 targets REVISED DOWN to +3%/+6% organic sales growth (vs ~+7% CAGR in the original GO-28 plan) with organic CEBIT growth 'above sales growth' (vs 'at least +10%') - framed as a worldwide healthcare-budget squeeze (defense spending, US 15% tariffs, ~$100 oil, AI-driven chip inflation), NOT a competitive deterioration: BIOFIRE/SPOTFIRE share and pricing assumptions from 2024 are tracking as planned.

SPOTFIRE delivered its best Q2 since launch (reagent sales +40%, 400 instruments installed with no one-offs, installed base 7,200 units, +60% vs June 2025) and the euro target of EUR 450M by 2028 is replaced by +25%/+40% growth vs 2026 (~EUR 400-410M - the gap is essentially FX); Japan now restricts the SPOTFIRE respiratory panel to 'high-risk patients', a structural headwind whose exact scope is still being defined.

China microbiology improving (-6% in H1 vs ~-15% in 2025) on instrument localization and the end of 2025 destocking; Danaher/Cepheid's announced high-plex system is read as a validation of the multiplex market (no panels disclosed yet); FY26 guidance confirmed (+3/+5% sales, 0/+10% CEBIT) with the bottom of the range if the Q4 respiratory season merely matches a weak Q4 25; H1 FCF nearly doubled to ~EUR 300M, net cash EUR 236M.

guidanceHistory.guidanceAnnuelle: Downward revision post-warning: organic revenue +3% to +5% (vs +5-7% before the warning); organic ROCC 0% to +10% (vs ≥10% before the warning); ROCC FX effect -50 to -60 M€.

FY2026 targets confirmed (organic revenue +3%/+5%; organic ROCC 0%/+10%); ROCC FX effect revised favourably to -40/-50 M€. 2027-2028 outlook adjusted down: organic revenue +3%/+6% per year (vs +7% CAGR previously); organic ROCC > revenue growth (vs ≥10% previously).

hypothese.guidanceLongTerme: GO•28 strategic plan (2028 horizon): four pillars - GO•Simple (operational efficiency), Grow Stronger (employee engagement), responsible growth (CSR, -35% Scope 3 emissions targeted by 2034), and four product growth drivers (non-respiratory BIOFIRE +4%/+8% per year 2027-2028, SPOTFIRE +25%/+40% per year, Microbiology +3%/+5% per year, Industrial Applications). Ambition for R&D at 12% of revenue by end-2028. Trajectory beyond 2028 not specified at this stage (management indicates that a new Capital Markets Day would be the appropriate setting in which to communicate it).
hypothese.summary: The H1 2026 refresh records a structural change of trajectory rather than a simple cyclical adjustment: the Q2 rebound (+5% organic) confirms that the Q1 warning was indeed tied to respiratory epidemiology and not to a loss of market share, but management takes the opportunity of the release to lower its 2027-2028 medium-term ambitions (organic revenue +3-6% vs +7% CAGR targeted previously), acknowledging a durably deteriorated macro/geopolitical environment. Cash generation remains a major strength (FCF +76% in H1, net cash position lifted to 236 M€).
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
World leader in syndromic/multiplex in-vitro diagnostics (BIOFIRE). The refresh marks a thesis inflection: what the April warning framed as conjunctural (weak respiratory season, BIOFIRE respiratory -23% organic in Q1) is now compounded by a structural mid-term cut announced at H1 - 2027-2028 organic revenue now guided +3% to +6%/yr (vs '+7% CAGR 2024-2028' before) and organic ROCC merely 'above revenue growth' (vs 'at least +10%'). FY26 guidance itself is confirmed (+3/+5% organic; ROCC 0/+10%) on a solid Q2 (+5% organic, +7.3% ex-respiratory).

== THESIS READ ==
- Mid-term de-rating is the story: the multiple now rests on GO*28 execution and BIOFIRE menu expansion, not a mechanical +7% top line. Watch: the first 2027 guidance (Feb 2027) under the new frame.
- FY26 pace is credible after Q2; the quarterly progression matched what management laid out. Watch: H2 respiratory season - the swing factor for the confirmed range.
- PPA bridge corrected: real acquired-intangible amortization runs ~28M/yr vs ~66M assumed at setup - the retreated base was too conservative and has been refined. Watch: residual REVEAL/restructuring charges polluting the bridge.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Data retreated for two true one-offs only (Hybiome 2023, VITEK REVEAL 2025); recurring PPA amortization and GO*28 restructuring deliberately KEPT in the base (rule E5e) - 'ebit' is published recurring operating income plus true one-offs, NOT management's contributive ROCC. Growing net cash position (-320M in 2026 to -720M in 2030) yields a small positive financial result in the bridge.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26: EBIT 677M on the confirmed guidance mid. 2027-2030: ~5%/yr revenue, margin drift +30-40bp/yr - aligned with the LOWERED mid-term frame, not the old +7% CAGR. Bridge: ETR 25%, positive finNet rising with net cash; published 2025 reconciles at zero residual on the retreated base. Shares flat at 118M. Watch: FX drag (-40/-50M on ROCC guided); US respiratory volumes; menu approvals cadence.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 sales (Oct); FY26 results (Feb 2027) with first 2027 guidance under the new frame; BIOFIRE menu approvals; GO*28 milestones.

ancrages.moteur: Official guidance confirmed at H1 2026 (28/07/2026) after the Q1 warning: organic revenue +3% to +5% for FY2026; taken at ~3,5% (close to the low end of the range), with management explicitly indicating that the central scenario (Q4 2026 respiratory season = Q4 2025, already weak) points towards the low end of the range.

FX effect estimated at around -150 M€ on FY2026 revenue (actual H1 2026 -87,3 M€ + prudent extrapolation of a more moderate effect in H2, consistent with the improvement in the FX guidance on ROCC from -50/-60 M€ to -40/-50 M€); the company gives no explicit FX guidance on revenue (only on ROCC).

2027-2028 outlook REVISED DOWN by the company itself at H1 2026: annual organic revenue growth targeted between +3% and +6% (vs '+7% CAGR 2024-2028' previously); taken at +5%/yr over 2027-2028 (close to the midpoint, consistent with the Q2 2026 pace that management recommends using as a reference); prudent extrapolation at +5%/yr for 2029-2030 in the absence of guidance beyond 2028 (the company itself indicates that a new Capital Markets Day would be needed to opine on that horizon).

Official guidance confirmed at H1 2026: organic ROCC 0% to +10% for FY2026; taken at ~3% (low end of the range, consistent with the prudent revenue assumption), ROCC FX effect -40/-50 M€ (of which -35 M€ already booked in H1 2026).

Guidance revised at H1 2026: organic ROCC growth simply targeted above that of revenue over 2027-2028 (vs '≥10%' previously); taken at around +1,5 pt above revenue growth each year (+6,5% in 2027, +6,5% in 2028 then a gradual moderation to +6%/2029 and +5,5%/2030), reflecting the accelerated GO•Simple initiatives (headcount reduction, site closure brought forward) intended to generate that operating leverage.

REVISED at this refresh (E6-a/E6-b): the ROCC/ROC(basis used) gap recalibrated to ≈28 M€ for 2026 (amortisation of acquired intangibles annualised on the basis of the actual H1 2026 figure of -14,2 M€), against ≈66 M€ estimated at the creation refresh - the old assumption appears in hindsight to have been overstated. Slight annual increase (+2 M€/yr) reflecting the integration of Accellix and of future bolt-on acquisitions.

Normative effective tax rate maintained at 23,4% (actual effective rate in H1 2026, consistent with the FY2025 rate of 24,5% judged clean - a slight downward revision relative to the assumption used at the creation refresh).

UNRESOLVED METHODOLOGICAL TENSION: a company in a growing net cash position with no active and regular buyback programme within the meaning of the protocol, which would mechanically point towards financial income at the 10-year Bund (3,20%) + 2 pts. But the actual H1 2026 net financial result is negative (-5 M€, vs +4 M€ in H1 2025), management attributing it to the adverse effect of the stronger euro on foreign-currency cash positions rather than to a structural lack of yield. Taken prudently close to zero in 2026 (-8 M€, extrapolation of the H1 pace) then a gradual and modest normalisation (0 M€ in 2027, +5/+8/+10 M€ in 2028-2030) rather than the theoretical Bund+2pts rate, which would give an appreciably higher result given the growing net cash - to be settled at the next refresh depending on whether or not the FX effect persists.

Partial impairment of VITEK REVEAL (146 M€ pretax reported, H1 2025) adjusted out of 2025 data (E5 d-bis); deductible tax treatment confirmed by the net income/adjusted net income reconciliation published by the company (theoretical tax effect of 34,9 M€ on the impairment, consistent with an effective tax rate close to 24%). Ex-post confirmation of the one-off nature of this event: amortisation of acquired intangibles returned to a normalised level of -14,2 M€ in H1 2026 (vs -163,2 M€ in H1 2025), with no new impairment.

Hybiome goodwill/technology impairment adjusted out of 2023 data (E5 d-bis); pretax amount ≈52 M€ reconstructed via the gap between the reported effective tax rate (26,2%) and the adjusted one (23,4%, explicitly declared by the company itself); non-deductible tax treatment confirmed explicitly by the company.

Diluted share count recalibrated to 118M (actual number at 30/06/2026: 118 367 846, slightly down vs 118 905 491 a year earlier); modest net buybacks in H1 2026 (-19,3 M€) judged insufficient to qualify as an active and regular buyback programme within the meaning of E5-a bis (see the financial result anchor).
